reproduction_target: Multi-omics study of IMR-90 human fibroblasts electroporated with an AluJb overexpression construct. Computational target: (a) RNA-seq of the AluJb-OE vs empty-vector experiment - fastp trimming, fastqc QC, STAR alignment to a GRCh38/GENCODE-44 reference modified with the plasmid as an extra contig, TEtranscripts TEcount gene + repeat-subfamily quantification against a dated Hammell-lab TE GTF, cpm filtering, DESeq2 differential expression, Spearman-distance MDS; (b) re-analysis of a public human aging fibroblast mRNA-seq dataset (GSE113957, 133 -> 82 -> 76 curated samples) with the same trimming/mapping stack plus TElocal locus-level counting, genomic-context aggregation, XIST/DDX3Y sex-marker QC, 1.5*IQR outlier removal, limma removeBatchEffect and DESeq2 across age; (c) DIA mass-spectrometry processing in Spectronaut directDIA (intracellular proteome and secretome) followed by paired t-test + Storey q-value differential abundance; (d) functional enrichment and network analysis - clusterProfiler GSEA, mitch multi-contrast enrichment, MSigDB 2024.1.Hs GO and Reactome v92 gene sets plus aging/senescence gene sets, Fisher's-method meta-ranking, mosaic-plot Fisher tests, decoupleR TF-activity inference with CollecTRI, and a NetworkAnalyst web-platform PPI/SIGNOR network; (e) analysis of functional assay data (Seahorse Mito Stress Test, propidium-iodide cell cycle, PROTEOSTAT aggresome) in R with Wilcoxon tests, and flow-cytometry gating in Flowlogic Solution 1.0. Cell culture, plasmid construction by overlap-extension PCR, electroporation, RNA extraction and library prep/sequencing, DIA-MS sample prep and acquisition, Seahorse/flow assay bench work and DNA gels are wet-lab (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis list built from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML full text. WebFetch on the .source.xml returned HTTP 403 and a first curl attempt hit Cloudflare error 1015 (rate limit); the XML was retrieved on a second curl attempt with a browser user-agent (200 OK, 184919 bytes) and tag-stripped locally. The paper has an explicit 'Data and code availability' section naming SRA BioProject PRJNA1008694, MassIVE MSV000097822 / ProteomeXchange PXD063739, a figshare DOI, and the GitHub repository https://github.com/BenayounLaboratory/AluJB_fibroblast_overexpression. Repo landing page and README.txt prose were read (Stage-1 permitted surfaces only): the repo has MIT LICENSE, README.txt, and four top-level analysis directories (1_Public_RNAseq_Meta-Analysis, 2_RNAseq_Analysis, 3_Mass_Spec_Analyses, 4_Functional_Data_Analyses) each with its own README; it has NO tag and NO release (GitHub /tags and /releases both return empty arrays), so the code artifact is a floating main branch (HEAD 8965286f05ea50d70155a1c33e18ffda47bdc836, pushed 2025-11-19). No lockfile, container, renv.lock or conda spec is claimed anywhere in the paper or in the top-level README. Prose pins are unusually good (fastp v0.20.1, fastqc v0.11.9, STAR v2.7.3a, TEtranscripts v2.1.4, TElocal v1.1.1, R v4.3.3, DESeq2 v1.42.1, limma v3.58.1, clusterProfiler v4.10.1, mitch v1.14.0, decoupleR v2.8.0, GENCODE 44, MSigDB 2024.1.Hs, Reactome v92, dated TE GTF downloads), and the paper states 'code was re-run independently on R version 4.3.3 to check for reproducibility' - but exact pins without environment closure cap version at 1 under rubric Delta-2, so no step can exceed RI on prose alone. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Read trimming of AluJb-OE RNA-seq with fastp v0.20.1: adapter removal, hard trim of first 15 bp, low-quality base removal, minimum length 36 bp
Post-trimming read QC with fastqc v0.11.9 (no invocation parameters stated; inspection is manual)

Construction of a modified reference: GRCh38 primary assembly + comprehensive annotation from GENCODE release 44, with the AluJb overexpression plasmid added as an extra contig (plasmid sequence itself is described in wet-lab prose, not deposited as a FASTA accession)
Alignment with STAR v2.7.3a to the modified genome, parameters outFilterMultimapNmax 100, winAnchorMultimapNmax 100, outFilterMismatchNoverLmax 0.04

Gene and repeat-subfamily quantification with TEcount from TEtranscripts v2.1.4, using GENCODE 44 gene boundaries and the Hammell-lab GRCh38_GENCODE_rmsk_TE.gtf.gz downloaded 2023-09-14 from labshare.cshl.edu (URL + download date given, no file checksum)
Low-expression filtering in R v4.3.3: cpm threshold corresponding to 10 reads in the median-length library, kept if exceeded in at least as many samples as the smallest group
Differential expression of genes and repeat subfamilies with DESeq2 v1.42.1 (FDR < 0.05) between AluJb-OE and empty vector
Multidimensional scaling of samples using a 1 - Spearman's rho distance matrix passed to the R 'cmdscale' function

Curation of the public human aging fibroblast mRNA-seq dataset (GSE113957, 133 donors): keep adults >= 20 y, self-reported 'Caucasian' ethnicity, arm-skin extraction site -> 82 samples; per-sample selection list is described in prose but no curated sample manifest accession is given

Trimming/mapping of the curated public dataset: fastp v0.20.1 with additional 3' hard trimming to equalise the two read lengths, then STAR v2.7.3a to the unmodified GRCh38/GENCODE-44 reference (the 3' trim length itself is not stated numerically)

Individual repeat-locus quantification with TElocal v1.1.1 using a prebuilt index downloaded 2023-10-31 from the Hammell-lab labshare directory (directory URL + date given, exact index file not named, no checksum)
Aggregation of repeat-locus counts by subfamily and genomic context (intronic, exon-overlapping, intergenic within 5 kb of a gene, intergenic > 5 kb), following a previously published categorisation

Sample QC of the public dataset: XIST / DDX3Y sex-marker check for mislabeling or cross-contamination plus 1.5*IQR outlier rule, removing 6 samples to yield 76 (the statistic to which the IQR rule is applied is not named)

Batch-effect regression on raw counts for biological sex and sequencing instrument with removeBatchEffect from limma v3.58.1, then DESeq2 v1.42.1 differential expression across age with a 20%-of-samples cpm expression filter

DIA-MS spectral processing in Spectronaut (versions 14.10.201222.47784 and 15.1.210713.50606) using directDIA against the UniProtKB-SwissProt human reference proteome (20,380 entries, accessed 2021-01-29), Trypsin/P, 2 missed cleavages, fixed Cys carbamidomethylation, variable Met oxidation and protein N-term acetylation, 1% precursor and protein q-value, XIC quantification on 3-6 b/y MS2 fragments, q-value sparse filtering + iRT profiling, local normalisation for cell pellets only

Differential protein abundance: paired t-test with Storey-method group-wise multiple-testing correction; intracellular significance at >= 2 unique peptides, q < 0.05, |log2FC| > 0.2; secretome at >= 2 unique peptides, q < 0.05, |log2FC| > 0.58

Gene set enrichment analysis with clusterProfiler v4.10.1 (fgsea paradigm), ranking transcriptomic results by DESeq2 Wald statistic and proteomic/secretomic results by log2FC * -log10(q), FDR < 0.05 significance

Gene set collections: GO from MSigDB release 2024.1.Hs, Reactome v92 pathway sets from the Reactome website, plus core SASP, SenMayo, CellAge build 3, GTEx-derived aging genes, and author-derived AluS up/down gene lists (release identifiers pinned; downloaded files not deposited or hashed)
Cross-omics multi-contrast pathway enrichment with mitch v1.14.0, significance at adjusted MANOVA p < 0.05

Gene-set meta-ranking and plotting rules: Fisher's-method combination of p-values across analyses, top-5 up / top-5 down selection with substitution when fewer than 5 exist, and Fisher-test mosaic plots of gene-set member abundance at p < 0.05

Transcription-factor activity inference with decoupleR v2.8.0 running the 'fgsea' algorithm on Wald-statistic-ranked genes against the CollecTRI regulon collection (CollecTRI snapshot version/date not stated), significance p < 0.05, top-5 up / top-5 down by magnitude

Gene network construction on the NetworkAnalyst web platform on 2025-05-15: FDR < 0.05 genes ranked by Wald statistic submitted as a gene list, union of a generic first-order STRING PPI network (confidence 900, experimental evidence required) and a SIGNOR 2.0 signaling network, visualising subnetwork 1 - no NetworkAnalyst version, no STRING release, interactive platform with no scripted invocation

Seahorse XF Mito Stress Test data parsing and analysis in R v4.3.3 (Parse_Seahorse_Excel / SUMMARY_Seahorse_Analysis scripts in repo dir 4): Hoechst-fluorescence cell-number normalisation, per-experiment normalisation to control median, combination across 2 experiments (n = 12 per group), Wilcoxon test p < 0.05

Cell-cycle (propidium iodide, n = 18 per group) and PROTEOSTAT aggresome (n = 24 per group) result analysis in R v4.3.3 (Analyze_Cell_Cycle_Results.R, Analyze_Proteostat_Results.R): per-experiment normalisation to control median, combination across experiments, Wilcoxon test p < 0.05

Flow-cytometry gating and quantification for the Proteostat and cell-cycle assays in Flowlogic Solution 1.0 (MACSQuant Analyzer 10 data) - version stated, but gating strategy is not described and the tool is a commercial GUI with no scripted invocation
Secretome frequency comparison of Alu-regulated vs non-regulated secreted proteins with Fisher's exact test, significance p < 0.05

headline.static_readiness: 0/26 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 23/26 computational steps (C1-C14 and C16-C21, C23, C24, C26: the fastp/fastqc/STAR/TEtranscripts/TElocal read-processing chain, cpm filtering, DESeq2 1.42.1 differential expression, Spearman MDS, public-dataset curation and batch regression with limma 3.58.1, DIA differential abundance, clusterProfiler 4.10.1 and mitch 1.14.0 enrichment, gene-set meta-ranking, decoupleR 2.8.0 TF activity, and the R-based Seahorse / cell-cycle / Proteostat / secretome statistics). This is an unusually well-pinned paper: essentially every locally run tool carries an exact version, reference resources carry release identifiers (GENCODE 44, MSigDB 2024.1.Hs, Reactome v92) or dated download URLs, raw data for all three omics layers plus the functional assays are publicly deposited (SRA PRJNA1008694, MassIVE MSV000097822, figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.28928147, plus public GSE113957 for the re-analysis), the analysis code is public and organised one directory per analysis, and the authors state the code was re-run independently on R 4.3.3 as a reproducibility check. It nevertheless cannot exceed RI at Stage 1 because there is NO environment closure claimed anywhere - no renv.lock, no conda/mamba environment file, no container image or digest, no sessionInfo export named in the paper or the top-level README - so the version axis is capped at 1 for every step under rubric Delta-2, and the repository carries no tag or release (floating main branch, HEAD 8965286f, pushed 2025-11-19). 3/26 steps cap at NI, all for the same structural reason: the step runs in a closed interactive tool with no scripted invocation - C15 Spectronaut directDIA (commercial GUI; full build strings pinned but no analysis schema deposited), C25 Flowlogic Solution 1.0 flow-cytometry gating (commercial GUI, gating strategy never described, params = 0), and C22 NetworkAnalyst (unversioned web platform used on 2025-05-15, STRING release not stated; version = 0 and code = 0). Three further steps stay at RI but carry the weakest inputs and are the ones most likely to fail a Stage-2 check: C3 (the AluJb plasmid contig added to the reference is not deposited as a sequence artifact), C18 (GMT files for the gene-set collections are pinned by release name but not deposited or hashed, and the derived AluS up/down lists are not published), and C21 (the CollecTRI regulon snapshot carries no version).
headline.coverage: 26 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML Methods prose plus the public GitHub landing page and README.txt prose (RNA-seq trimming/mapping/TE quantification and differential expression; curation and re-analysis of the public aging fibroblast dataset GSE113957 including locus-level TElocal counting and batch regression; DIA-MS processing and differential protein abundance for intracellular proteome and secretome; GSEA / multi-contrast enrichment / TF-activity / network analysis; functional-assay statistics). 9 wet-lab step groups counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope: IMR-90 culture and STR/mycoplasma verification; AluJb construct assembly by overlap-extension PCR and cloning into pLKO.1/pUC19; electroporation transfection and recovery; RNA extraction, ScreenTape RIN QC, Novogene unstranded mRNA library prep and NovaSeq 6000 PE150 sequencing; DIA-MS sample preparation and LC-MS acquisition (cell pellets and secretome); Agilent Seahorse XF Mito Stress Test bench assay; propidium-iodide staining and fixation; PROTEOSTAT aggresome staining; MACSQuant flow-cytometry acquisition and DNA gel imaging.

gaps.where: Whole software environment (fastp/fastqc/STAR/TEtranscripts/TElocal command-line stack and the R 4.3.3 Bioconductor stack: DESeq2, limma, clusterProfiler, mitch, decoupleR)
gaps.missing: No environment closure of any kind is claimed. The Methods contain an 'Other software versions' subsection stating only 'Analyses were conducted using R version 4.3.3 and code was re-run independently on R version 4.3.3 to check for reproducibility.' There is no renv.lock, no DESCRIPTION/requirements file, no conda or mamba environment.yml, no container image or digest, and no sessionInfo() export named in the paper or in the repository's top-level README.txt. Exact prose pins exist for nearly every tool, which is why the paper classifies as exact_pins_partial rather than floating, but pins without closure cap the version axis at 1 for all 26 computational steps.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship an renv.lock (or conda-lock / pixi lockfile) covering R 4.3.3 plus DESeq2 1.42.1, limma 3.58.1, clusterProfiler 4.10.1, mitch 1.14.0 and decoupleR 2.8.0, and a container digest or conda spec for the command-line stack (fastp 0.20.1, fastqc 0.11.9, STAR 2.7.3a, TEtranscripts 2.1.4, TElocal 1.1.1). Commit the lockfile into the analysis repository and reference it from the Data and code availability statement.

gaps.missing: The repository is public, MIT-licensed and well organised (four analysis directories each with its own README), but it carries NO tag and NO release - the GitHub tags and releases endpoints both return empty arrays - and the paper cites the bare repository URL with no commit SHA. The code artifact the manuscript refers to is therefore a moving main branch (HEAD 8965286f05ea50d70155a1c33e18ffda47bdc836 as of 2025-11-19, repository created 2025-07-06), which is not a fixed reproduction target.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release for the manuscript version and archive it to Zenodo for a DOI, then cite the tag/DOI (not the bare repository URL) in the Data and code availability statement.

gaps.where: C22 (NetworkAnalyst web platform), C21 (CollecTRI regulon collection), C15 (Spectronaut), C25 (Flowlogic)
gaps.missing: NetworkAnalyst is used interactively on a stated date (2025-05-15) with no platform version and no STRING release identifier (only a confidence cutoff of 900 and 'experimental evidence'); SIGNOR is pinned at 2.0. The CollecTRI regulon collection used by decoupleR carries no version or snapshot date. Spectronaut is pinned to two full build strings but is a commercial closed-source GUI, and Flowlogic Solution 1.0 is likewise a commercial GUI whose gating strategy is never described. These four steps cannot be re-executed from the published artifacts even in principle.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the NetworkAnalyst platform version and STRING release used (or replace the interactive step with a scripted STRINGdb query at a pinned release), state the CollecTRI snapshot version, deposit the Spectronaut analysis schema/settings file alongside the MassIVE submission, and publish the flow-cytometry gating strategy plus the exported gate definitions.

gaps.where: C2 (fastqc), C3 (plasmid contig), C9 (public-sample curation), C10 (3' hard trim), C11 (TElocal index), C13 (IQR outlier rule)
gaps.missing: Parameter and input under-specification at six points. (i) fastqc is version-pinned but no invocation is given and 'read quality was inspected' is a manual judgement. (ii) The modified reference includes 'the sequence for the AluJb overexpression plasmid as an additional contig' but that contig FASTA is not deposited in any accession - it must be reconstructed from the wet-lab cloning description. (iii) The curated 82-sample subset of the 133-donor public dataset is defined by prose criteria (age >= 20, 'Caucasian', arm skin) with no deposited sample manifest, and the 6 samples removed by the 1.5*IQR rule are not listed nor is the statistic the rule was applied to named. (iv) The 3' hard-trim length used to equalise the two read lengths in the public data is not stated numerically. (v) The TElocal prebuilt index is cited by directory URL and download date only, without naming the exact index file or a checksum; the same applies to the TE GTF in C5.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the modified reference FASTA (or at minimum the plasmid contig sequence) and the curated sample manifest with per-sample keep/drop flags and the outlier statistic; state the fastqc invocation and the numeric 3' trim length; record the exact filenames plus sha256 of the downloaded TE GTF and TElocal index.

gaps.missing: Gene set collections are pinned by release name (MSigDB 2024.1.Hs, Reactome v92) and by citation (core SASP, SenMayo, CellAge build 3, GTEx aging genes, AluS up/down lists derived from a prior publication), but no downloaded GMT files are deposited or hashed, and the AluS up/down lists are constructed by the authors as the union of up- and of down-regulated genes across two prior overexpression conditions without the resulting lists being published as a supplementary artifact.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the exact GMT files used (or their sha256) alongside the code, and publish the derived AluS upregulated / downregulated gene lists as a supplementary table.
